channel.title: Halt updates
channel.description: New versions of Halt for Windows. Written by tools\Publish-Release.ps1.

item.title: Halt 0.12.1
item.description:
• Halt opens in its own window, named Halt with Halt's icon, from the first moment. Before, it opened in an Edge window that showed "127.0.0.1" and Edge's icon while it started.
  • When you add a site, Halt checks the address. If it now opens a different site (twitter.com opens x.com), Halt offers to add that one too, because a block on the old address doesn't cover it. If the address doesn't exist, Halt says so. Custom bundles are checked when you save them.
  • Changed: Halt has a new icon: a white hourglass on a violet tile, sharp at every size from the tray to the Start menu. The browser extension gets it too.
  • Changed: The tray menu (right-click on Halt's icon by the clock) is drawn in Halt's colors and stays sharp at any display scaling, with the session's time left at the top. Before, it was a blurry grey Windows menu.
  • Changed: The Block tab shows Apps to close right under your blocked sites, with the apps found on this PC below the add box and a button for every installed app.
  • Changed: The settings password card says what the password guards, and once one is set it offers Change and Remove instead of two empty boxes. Turning off the Password lock switch now opens Remove right there.
  • Changed: Adding to a block no longer asks for the settings password: a site, an app, a Shorts or Reels block, or switching on app blocking. Blocking more never helps anyone get around Halt, and with the Password lock someone else keeps the password, so a site you forgot can now be added mid-session. Removing or loosening anything still asks for it.
  • Changed: The Social bundle now has threads.com (Threads moved there from threads.net), and News has bbc.co.uk. Existing settings get them once, and a block list with twitter.com gets x.com too.
  • Changed: With the browser extension 2.1.0, a site over its daily limit shows Halt's page saying when it opens again, instead of "You're in a focus session". A site blocked by a school's or employer's policy keeps the browser's own page.
  • Changed: With the browser extension 2.1.0, blocking also covers moves inside a site that don't load a new page (a blocked youtube.com/@name or reddit.com/r/all reached by clicking around YouTube or Reddit, another video in allowlist mode), and tabs that were already open when a session or a daily limit started (switched to Halt's page within a minute). Halt's page offers the site again as soon as Halt stops blocking it, for example on a break.
  • Changed: The quick-add apps under "Apps to close" and in a new app limit are now apps found on your PC, with the ones open right now first: launchers, chat apps and your Steam, Epic and Riot games. Before, it was a fixed list.
  • Fixed: Removing every app, or turning off every Shorts/Reels switch, no longer stops you from adding sites during a session. An empty list was saved in a way that later read back as a fake entry.
  • Fixed: Empty lists stay empty after a session starts and stops, and settings already affected by that load correctly again.
  • Fixed: Typing a site, a time or a text length into a new daily limit now saves. Before, the form ignored what you typed.
  • Fixed: The app picker no longer offers parts of Windows (such as the Edge engine other apps run in) or installers and uninstallers.
  • Fixed: The hourglass grains now shrink with the glass, so the small 1h glass no longer looks coarse.
  • Fixed: Clicking a switch on a Protection card no longer makes the card jump.
  • Fixed: The Password lock card now shows whether a settings password is set, and its switch takes you to the password field. Before, it was a switch that did nothing.
  • Fixed: After an update with no release notes, the notice no longer shows "What’s new: null".
  • Removed: Old hidden instructions for loading the browser extension by hand; it installs from the Chrome and Edge stores now.

item.title: Halt 0.12.0
item.description:
• Unlock Halt Pro with the email you paid with: in Settings, press "I already bought it", enter your email and type the 6-digit code we send you. No key to copy, and a new PC or a reinstall takes a few seconds. Pasting a license key still works.
  • Halt Pro now works on all the PCs you use, with no 3-PC limit: each one is unlocked with your email.
  • Fixed: Clicking the Halt icon while Halt is already open brings its window to the front instead of opening a second window, even right after it starts.
  • Fixed: The last site in your block list can now be removed (it used to come back).
  • Fixed: "Instagram Reels" now also blocks Instagram's Explore page, where Reels open as posts.

item.title: Halt 0.11.1
item.description:
• Settings has a "My purchase" button for Halt Pro: it opens haltmode.com/account, where you can email yourself your key, remove a PC you no longer use, or refund Halt Pro yourself within 30 days.
  • Changed: When a license has been added to many different PCs recently, Halt now says new PCs open up again by themselves, and how to free a place sooner.

item.title: Halt 0.11.0
item.description: • Buy Halt Pro right from the app: "Get Halt Pro" opens the checkout in your browser, and once you have paid, Halt switches to Pro by itself within a few seconds. There is no key to copy.

item.title: Halt 0.10.0
item.description:
• Blocks the websites you choose in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox, including private windows, using the browsers' own policy settings.
  • Closes blocked apps and games within 2 seconds of opening, with a short message saying why.
  • Locks: a timer lock in Halt Basic, and in Halt Pro a wait, a long random text, a restart, or a password someone else keeps.
  • Schedules that start blocks on their own, plus breaks and daily allowances.
  • Adult content filter for the whole PC with SafeSearch locked, a cool-down you set in advance, and a Permanent mode.
  • One switch to block YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and Facebook Reels.
  • Stats, a weekly challenge and one-tap site bundles.
  • Halt Pro licenses, activated on up to 3 PCs.
  • Automatic updates: Halt checks for a new version once a day and installs it when no session is running, without changing your settings.
  • Lock this PC (Halt Pro): keeps the whole computer on the Windows lock screen for a time you choose, up to 12 hours, even after a restart. There is no early stop, and Safe Mode always lets you back in.
  • Light mode: choose Dark, Light, or System (follows Windows) in Settings > Theme.
  • Halt waits in the tray by the clock when its window is closed or minimized, with the session's countdown in the tooltip; click the icon to open it again. Off in Settings > Start-up and tray if you prefer.
  • Start with Windows (off by default): Halt opens in the tray when you sign in, with no window and no admin prompt.
  • A slimmer hourglass frame: rounded metal rods and capped discs, lit, and the glass sways instead of spinning.
  • The hourglass's sand is your session's time: one grain for every second, and one grain falls each second, so the sand at the bottom is exactly the time that has passed.
  • Daily time limits (Halt Pro): cap how long you use a site, app or bundle each day, for example YouTube for 2 hours or Spotify for 6. When you reach the cap it's blocked for the rest of the day, and only the lock you chose (timer, delay, text, restart or password) can lift it early. A site counts while it's the tab in front of you, an app while it's in front or playing sound (so music counts), and time away from the PC doesn't. Limits reset at midnight and run all day without a focus session. There's a new Limits tab.
  • Block a single page, channel or playlist, not just a whole site: add an entry like youtube.com/@name or youtube.com/watch?list=... to your blocked or allowed list.
  • Block Task Manager and the Command Prompt during a focus session (Halt Pro), so a session can't simply be killed. It's switched off in Settings by default, clears the moment the session ends, and never gets in the way of uninstalling Halt.
  • A free 7-day Halt Pro trial: the first install on a PC unlocks everything for 7 days, with no card and no account. After that Halt keeps working as Halt Basic, and the Pro settings you made wait for a license. The header shows the days left, and the trial runs once per PC, even after reinstalling.
  • Halt opens without the Windows admin prompt. The Halt service now runs the part that changes protected settings, and the app window runs with your normal rights. "Start with Windows" works the same way.
